policy: Every statically registered Hono operation, including local and imported string constants, is either a supported public automation operation in OpenAPI or matches exactly one narrow exclusion family below; dynamic or unresolvable route registration fails closed.

exclusions.rationale: The playground uses an ephemeral cookie-bound browser session and is not a stable third-party automation contract.
These are static assets, human or agent-readable documentation, discovery metadata, or the OpenAPI representation itself rather than callable REST operations.
These endpoints implement the value-free interactive CLI authorization ceremony and are intentionally driven by the first-party CLI and browser.
WorkOS login, callback, account switching, and logout are cookie-bound browser identity ceremonies rather than public REST automation.
The WordPress and external-review bridge is a first-party origin-bound protocol with installation and browser-session checks, not a general REST surface.
These aggregate authenticated dashboard, account, and support-readiness models specifically for the first-party application shell.
This authenticated, credential-stripped metadata lookup only assists the first-party URL publishing form and is not a supported public automation contract.
The return endpoint consumes a flow-bound trusted-host cookie and is not an independently callable OAuth or deployment API.

Legacy package, revision, deployment, and provider-control routes remain only as repository-internal compatibility contracts and are deliberately absent from public documentation and Code Mode discovery.
Permanent deletion remains an owner-only first-party lifecycle action with a separate recovery-window contract, not a published automation promise.
Notification and flat feedback feeds are cookie-bound aggregate models for the global inbox and feedback pages.
Quarantine release and custom-MCP approval routes require an explicit trusted human ceremony and cannot be delegated as ordinary API operations.
These immutable JavaScript and CSS responses implement the trusted review host and artifact broker boundary rather than REST operations.
These authenticated exact-revision frame responses are opaque sandbox children of the documented trusted preview host, not independently supported automation operations.
Bootstrap endpoints are narrowly authenticated operational compatibility tools and are intentionally excluded from supported public automation.
These operations render application pages, sandboxed frames, trusted review hosts, or form actions and are governed by browser behavior specifications.
Organization, team, and invitation creation is a first-party WorkOS-backed administrative flow with human consent and role checks.
The legacy publish form and hostname status route remain supported for compatibility while new automation uses the revisioned public API.
Mentions, watches, invitations, and presence are interactive review state bound to a browser reviewer and canonical project authorization.
Ownership transition requests require a signed-in human confirmation ceremony and are intentionally not exposed as ordinary automation.
Managed platform reservation and retirement are release-fenced lifecycle-operator ceremonies with explicit human confirmation, not general automation operations.
